name: Executive order of May 17, 1884 changing the Navajo Reservation (Utah addition; New Mexico townships relinquished)
promises: Royce records that the order set apart an addition to the Navajo Reservation bounded by the Colorado and San Juan rivers and the Utah line (area 655).

Royce records that the order relinquished townships south of the San Juan River in New Mexico that the January 6, 1880 order had added (area 658); they were added back by executive order of April 24, 1886.
today: Royce records that a later order modified this one so that the lands it described west of 110 degrees west longitude and within Utah were restored to the public domain. That later order is a separate event.

openQuestions: This order both enlarged and reduced an executive-order reservation; under the project rule an executive-order reduction alone is not a breach, and no court, Commission or government finding about this land and order was located. The Navajo Commission dockets (229) concern aboriginal title, a different event.
The scanned Royce schedule is jumbled; the date of the later Utah restoration order was not read cleanly.
The Navajo Nation's own account of the 1884 order was not located.
